prompt_en: Photograph a complex working scene with color and material relationships made visibly readable in a maritime model workshop during exhibition loading. A woman with the supplied photograph's visible facial appearance and hair is the model conservator: preserve the visible facial proportions, brown eyes, short dark bob and light wispy bangs. Her fictional role and circumstances are invented for this photograph. She is guiding a repaired boat model into a fitted open carrying cradle. The hull has just cleared a folded support pad, and the shaped recess waits directly beneath it; a detached display-label holder and the pad lie beside the cradle, making the change from repair bench to transport legible. Her right hand cups the stern underside and her left palm supports the bow underside, both hands connected to relaxed bent forearms as she leans a little over the bench. Her feet stand on the workshop floor; the cradle rests flat on the table. Her attention follows the narrow gap below the hull, with quiet poise and a soft, absorbed expression. Color belongs to each identifiable object's own surface, and material remains a separate visible property. The large work apron is aubergine violet matte woven linen, with soft diffuse shading and visible fibers at the waist folds. The boat model hull repeats aubergine violet in smooth glossy lacquer over wood; a thin pale reflection bends along its curved flank while the underlying violet pigment remains legible. An ivory painted cabin and pale wooden deck identify the repaired object as a boat model. A slim warm-gold metal gunwale trim runs around the model's deck edge, with tiny upright railing posts that emphasize its delicate perimeter during the transfer. Along the boat's gunwale, the declared metallic trim has bounded colored reflections separate from the larger local-color field of the violet hull and linen apron. On the slender gold rail posts, highlight variation follows the trim surface while neighboring matte regions retain their own color: narrow specular glints follow the metal curvature, while the adjacent violet linen holds soft diffuse folds. A small ceramic hardware cup on the bench is yellow ochre under a glassy glaze, its hard rounded highlight distinct from the linen's diffuse shading and the lacquer's elongated reflection. The open collar and sleeves of her plain shirt are warm ivory cotton. These violet surfaces carry the large color areas, the ochre cup makes a smaller contrasting accent, and ivory surfaces leave breathing room around them. A small cloth work mat is woven with thin alternating violet and ivory stripes, the pattern contained within the mat's edge; the apron, hull and cup have continuous solid-color surfaces. Brushed steel repair tools and a raw pale-wood bench retain their own material colors. Broad window daylight keeps skin, ivory cloth and steel neutral, while gloss changes the highlights locally on the painted hull and glazed cup. The photograph's restrained neutral rendering lets the actual pigments carry the violet-and-ochre complementary pairing. A landscape medium-wide documentary photograph from a three-quarter position at chest height includes her face, both supporting hands, the entire boat and cradle, and enough shelving to read the model workshop. Use a natural perspective and moderate depth of field: the face, material comparison and the cradle gap remain clear, while distant stored hulls soften. The emotional center is the careful transfer of something just made whole, with the different colored surfaces supporting that one connected moment.
